# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b82 — Passive PID learning (opt-in adaptation)

Beta82 adds **non-invasive plant identification** to existing per-device PID controllers. It learns from normal, controller-owned heat/cool/dry cycles without deliberately turning hardware ON/OFF to identify it. Beta81's room-centric configuration, translations and all previously verified power, occupancy, window, compressor, sleep and recovery guards are preserved.

## Per-device PID adaptation

An additional **PID · Passive adaptation** selector appears on each managed device with a supported native PID capability:

- **Observe and suggest** (default): watches only eligible natural operating cycles; the existing Kp/Ki/Kd remain unchanged.
- **Bounded auto-adapt** (explicit opt-in): when the device is safely OFF and an independently consistent, high-confidence plant model is available, automatically moves Kp and Ki by **at most 10% in one application**, **no more than once every 24 hours**, and only after at least two further newly verified cycles between updates. The derivative gain Kd remains unchanged automatically; the SIMC/Lambda PI recommendation reports Kd = 0.
- **Disabled**: no passive observations.

The **Controller status** sensor exposes the current mode, confidence level, accepted-cycle count, identified process gain, time constant and dead time, and proposed **Kp/Ki/Kd**. Only short aggregated evidence from the last six qualifying cycles is persisted; raw time-series measurements and incomplete cycles stay in memory.

## Confidence and safety

- The observer requires a **single, recent physical temperature or humidity feedback sensor**; a stable explicit heat/cool/dry mode and target; a continuous OFF baseline; a complete, verified controller-owned OFF→ON→OFF cycle; and sustained first-order response with a measurable plateau.
- **A climate mode of HEAT alone is not physical activity evidence.** Climate hardware must explicitly report its actual \`hvac_action\` as heating/cooling/drying during an observed ON phase. Unowned/manual starts, stale/unknown data, fan-speed changes, windows/sleep holds, unknown/restarted phases, short ramps and inconsistent responses are discarded.
- SIMC/Lambda gains are computed from validated first-order-plus-dead-time models. A minimum of three consistent cycles is required for suggestions; **five independent, high-quality cycles** with holdout stability are required for high confidence. Unidentifiable, weak or unsafe models never produce executable recommendations.
- An automatic gain update uses the *same per-controller write lock* as manual edits, checks live source and room authority, all existing PID and compressor interlocks, absence of in-flight commands and positive evidence that the physical device is OFF **twice** before saving. No independent actuation is added; the existing PID scheduler and physical dwell decisions remain authoritative. Concurrent manual edits, changed device identity or stale proposals stop the gain change.
- Every proposed gain change has a stored prior-gains snapshot. Restarts do not resume incomplete response cycles or silently perform automatic updates.
- Initially supports verifiable, binary ON/OFF heating/cooling/drying feedback. It does **not** infer modulation capacity or make claims about an unmeasured variable-speed fan, appliance or thermostat.

## Validation

The version-gated release suite checks synthetic heating and humidity cycles, cooling/drying sign handling, plateau rejection, a running/unowned physical device, exact source identity, persistence, model confidence, manual-vs-auto behavior, 10% rate limits and 24-hour cooldown, real production authorization and double validation, 38 bundled language catalogs, PID, relay/compresser dwell, room occupancy, sleep, offline supply recovery, HA event stream and real Chromium dashboard regressions.

## Installation

Update the **existing** Home Environment Manager in HACS to **v0.6.0b82**, restart Home Assistant and hard-refresh the dashboard. Open the managed controller's entities, set its Control method to PID and select one explicit native heating/cooling/drying direction with a valid room feedback sensor. The new **PID · Passive adaptation** select defaults to **Observe and suggest**. To permit bounded gain updates after enough confirmed natural cycles, explicitly choose **Bounded auto-adapt**. No new physical devices or relays are created by this feature.
